Our application already uses a `Gtk::HeaderBar` instead of
a 'normal' window titlebar. The header bar is a direct child of the window,
and its type is `titlebar`. This is set in the
`window.ui` file.

Here we'll just make two small changes to the header bar. The `decoration-layout`
property is set in the `window.ui` file, to show only the close
button, and hide the minimize and maximize buttons. We also include an icon in the
resource file, and set up this icon as the window icon.
In `ExampleAppWindow`'s constructor:
Here is how the application now looks:

The `window.ui` file sets a header bar title, but this title is not shown.
That's because the stack switcher is a child of type `title`. The stack
switcher becomes a custom title that hides the title label.
